root_idea.summary: The evidence preserves three distinct lexical branches under these radicals: smoke, a snake, and a person without a spouse. The Quranic form belongs to the marital branch.
root_idea.development: Within the marital branch, the basic state of having no spouse extends to widowhood and remaining unmarried, with derived forms expressing causation, continued singleness, or marriage to a previously spouse-less woman. The smoke and snake branches are lexically distinct homonymous developments.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form أَيِّم; the Quran occurrence is its plural أَيَامَى.

senses.definition: A person without a spouse—especially a woman without a husband, and also a man without a wife.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is plural أَيَامَى. It can include those who have never married as well as those who have lost a spouse, and the lexical evidence applies it to both women and men.
A reported interpretation of the plural in Quran 24:32, according to which أَيَامَى denotes free women rather than, or in addition to, people without spouses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smoke; to smoke a bee-hive so that the bees leave it and the honey may be taken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical branch distinct from the marital and snake branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A snake, described in one account as white and identified in another with the jinn-snake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical branch distinct from the marital branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be without a spouse, including to become widowed or to remain unmarried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a woman without a husband or a man without a wife. The Form V usage can specify remaining some time without marrying; an idiom also describes the loss of a wife and cattle, with resulting strong desire for milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to have no spouse; to make a woman a widow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The widow-making sense is specifically associated with killing her husband.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take as wife a woman who has no husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is characterized as an أَيِّم at the time of marriage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A contraction meaning “what thing?” in an interrogative expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a particle-like contraction of أَيُّ مَا, not the marital lexical branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose wife has died, or a woman whose husband has died.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the paired expression أَيْمَانُ عَيْمَانُ / أَيْمَى عَيْمَى, the term is associated with the death or loss of both spouse and cattle, leaving a strong desire for milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female relation, such as a daughter, sister, or maternal aunt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: أَيَامَى is also reported as a plural for female relations in this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of widowing; said of war that kills men and leaves wives without husbands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional descriptive noun for the effect of war on married women.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rich or financially sufficient woman who has no husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The wealth or sufficiency qualification is part of this specialized lexical usage.

cautions: The Quranic plural أَيَامَى in 24:32 has a reported alternative interpretation as “free women” in addition to the ordinary lexical interpretation of people without spouses.
The root-level sources distinguish the marital, smoke, and snake branches as separate lexical lines; the latter two are not Quranic meanings of أَيَامَى.
